t: You are at the site of Bartlett's Buildings, once also called Bartlett's Court. It was a street off Holborn Circus, known for the number of lawyers who had offices there. It was a cul-de-sac, with an alley called Bartlett's Passage running west to Fetter Lane. An air raid destroyed it in 1941, during the Second World War. Walter Debenham Sweeting, who lived from 1839 to 1913, lived here. He was a clergyman, a headmaster at King's School, Peterborough, and a church historian.
